classification.difficultyReason: Select equal-side or equal-angle triangle properties, combine them with triangle angle sums, and solve short linear equations. The joined triangles require routine linked deductions.

content.prompt: This question reviews isosceles and equilateral triangles. Find the angles and sides marked with pronumerals, giving reasons.

spec.description: Tall isosceles triangle ABC with matching double ticks on AB and BC. Ordinary source-blue marks use house black.
spec.mathematics: AB=BC; angle C=80 degrees; angle A=alpha; angle B=beta.

answer.worked:
The base angles of isosceles $\triangle ABC$ are equal, so $\alpha=80^\circ$.

Using the angle sum of $\triangle ABC$:
$$\begin{align*}\beta&=180^\circ-80^\circ-80^\circ\\\beta&=20^\circ\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Left-pointing triangle CAB with equal sides CA and CB. Ordinary source-blue marks use house black.
spec.mathematics: CA=CB; angle C=40 degrees; angles A and B are alpha and beta.

answer.worked:
The base angles of isosceles $\triangle ABC$ are equal, so $\alpha=\beta$.

Using the triangle angle sum:
$$\begin{align*}2\alpha+40^\circ&=180^\circ\\2\alpha&=140^\circ\\\alpha&=70^\circ\end{align*}$$
Thus $\beta=70^\circ$.

spec.description: Inverted triangle LMN with two given equal angles and labelled sloping sides. Ordinary source-blue marks use house black.

answer.worked:
Equal angles in $\triangle LMN$ have equal opposite sides, so $MN=LN$.
$$\begin{align*}2x+7&=11\\2x&=4\\x&=2\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Triangles PQR and QRS share QR; all four marked segments retain double ticks and Q has a right angle below QR. Ordinary source-blue marks use house black.
spec.mathematics: PQ=PR=QR=QS; angle RQS=90 degrees; angle QPR=alpha; angle QSR=beta.

answer.worked:
$PQ=PR=QR$, so $\triangle PQR$ is equilateral and $\alpha=60^\circ$.

$QR=QS$, so the base angles of right isosceles $\triangle QRS$ are equal.
$$\begin{align*}2\beta+90^\circ&=180^\circ\\2\beta&=90^\circ\\\beta&=45^\circ\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Triangle KLM with all three angles labelled alpha and three side expressions. No side ticks are added. Ordinary source-blue marks use house black.
spec.mathematics: All angles equal alpha; KL=3y; KM=x; LM=6.

answer.worked:
Using the triangle angle sum:
$$\begin{align*}3\alpha&=180^\circ\\\alpha&=60^\circ\end{align*}$$
All three angles are equal, so $\triangle KLM$ is equilateral. Hence $x=6$ and
$$\begin{align*}3y&=6\\y&=2\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Two isosceles triangles share horizontal TU, with double ticks above and triple ticks below. Ordinary source-blue marks use house black.
spec.mathematics: RT=RU; TS=US; angle RTU=50 degrees; angle TUS=70 degrees; unknowns alpha at RUT, beta at UTS, gamma at TSU.

answer.short:
$\alpha=50^\circ$, $\beta=70^\circ$, $\gamma=40^\circ$.

Use the equal base angles in each isosceles triangle, then the triangle angle sum.
answer.worked:
$RT=RU$, so the base angles of isosceles $\triangle TRU$ are equal: $\alpha=50^\circ$.

$TS=US$, so the base angles of isosceles $\triangle STU$ are equal: $\beta=70^\circ$.

Using the angle sum of $\triangle STU$:
$$\begin{align*}\gamma&=180^\circ-70^\circ-70^\circ\\\gamma&=40^\circ\end{align*}$$
